title: Relaychain passdown journal (on-call quick playbook)
content:
Context / purpose:
This is a lightweight, personal passdown for the person taking over the 19:00-03:00 relay. Not a canonical runbook — quick hits, recent oddities, and short-term mitigations that have worked.

State summary (as of evening sweep):
- Hosted API p95 latency up to ~320ms last hour (baseline 200ms). CPU on frontends healthy, but several worker pods showing GC spikes and elevated GPU memory churn on node-gpua-04.
- Dedicated pool ‘dp-eu-west-1-s’ at 85% utilization, autoscaler recently bumped to +1 but plateaued.
- One degraded model-variant (gpt-redwood-quant-v2) flagged with higher reject rate — rollback to v1 will be painful (non-backwards compatible cache keys).
- No open pagers other than a noisy alert (high kvcache-miss-rate) that flapped 3x today.

Immediate actions to consider during your first 15 minutes:
1) Check the health dash: https://console.redwood/ops/dashboards/latency - focus on hosted/api p95 and pool utilization.
2) Tail runtime logs on the suspect node: ssh relay@node-gpua-04 && sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f --since "10 minutes ago". Look for repeated "KV cache mismatch" or OOM killer entries.
3) If kvcache-miss-rate > 15% for an endpoint, try warming prefix cache by re-running the last top-10 prompts (stored run: s3://ops-cache-warmers/latest.json). This is a bandaid.
4) If GPU memory churn / OOMs: cordon node-gpua-04: kubectl cordon node-gpua-04 && then drain non-critical pods: kubectl drain node-gpua-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force. Notify infra on Slack.

Commands I use frequently (copy-paste friendly):
- Tail API logs: kubectl -n hosted logs -l app=hosted-api --tail=200 -f
- Check pool utilization: redwoodctl pool describe dp-eu-west-1-s --metrics
- Restart runtime on a node (safe sequence): sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime && sleep 30 && sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 --no-pager
- Toggle routing fallback to cheaper region: redwoodctl routing set-policy --route hosted-api --policy fallback-region=us-west-2 --priority=low
- Rollback model variant (WARNING: cache invalidation): redwoodctl model rollback gpt-redwood-quant-v2 --target gpt-redwood-v1 --invalidate-cache=no

Recent incidents and notes (lessons learned):
- 2025-10-28: High p95 due to batching bug introduced in release 0.9.14. Fix: revert batching.opt-in flag; follow-up PR #2456 to add canary gating on B/E ratio.
- 2025-10-31: Cache corruption traced to mismatch between compile artifacts after cross-region deploy. Temporary mitigation was to clear KV prefix for affected endpoints and re-warm. Added an alert "kvcache-inconsistent" that triggers ops when miss spikes > 20%.

Temporary mitigations that helped earlier tonight:
- Lower request concurrency in the routing layer for the noisy endpoint: redwoodctl route update hosted-api/stream --concurrency 6 (reduced 12 -> 6). Saw immediate p95 improvement ~40ms.
- Forced model fallback to cpu-quantized variant for non-SLA customer traffic: redwoodctl policy set fallback-mode=quantized-cpu --target non-sla --duration 30m. Use sparingly.

Escalation map (quick):
- Tier 1 (this doc / you): quick triage, short-term mitigations above.
- Tier 2 (on-call infra): Liam Nguyen (pager/Slack DM) — node-level, kube, SSH fixes.
- Tier 3 (runtime + model ops): Priya Rao — model rollback, cache invalidation guidance, compile artifact fixes.
- Exec/CS alert if customer impact > 5% of tokens for 30+ minutes.

Open TODOs / unresolved things to flag to next shift:
- Confirm whether the autoscaler metric window is misconfigured (observed short spikes ignored). Ticket: JIRA-ENG-4218.
- Investigate repeated GC pauses in runtime at ~03:00 UTC — might be telemetry job overlapping with peak.
- Add a canary check for prefix-caching on deploys (notes started in PR #2482 but not finished).

Runbook snippets (draft) — copy these into a proper runbook if they help:
- Hot restart (runtime) when latency is high but no OOMs: sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime on the node with high latency, then run smoke test: curl -s -X POST https://hosted.redwood/api/v1/health/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq .latency
- Clear kvcache for endpoint E (manual step, destructive): redwoodctl kvcache clear --prefix "ep:/hosted-api/endpoint/E" --confirm && then re-warm using s3 warmers.
- Scale dedicated pool temporarily: redwoodctl pool scale dp-eu-west-1-s --replicas 3 (make sure budget approval for >2x scale if using reserved instances).

Handy links & dashboards (save to bookmarks):
- Ops latency dashboard: https://console.redwood/ops/dashboards/latency
- Pool utilization: https://console.redwood/ops/pools/dp-eu-west-1-s
- KV cache telemetry: https://console.redwood/ops/kvcache/metrics
- Recent deploys: https://console.redwood/ops/deploys?env=prod

Personal notes / shorthand for next person:
- If you see a new alert named "runtime-batch-failure", 9/10 it's the 0.9.14 batching flag — revert local gate first.
- Avoid full cache clear if you can re-warm (clearing causes token cost spike and customer annoyance).
- When draining nodes, prefer scale-up of pool first if traffic is high; draining causes cold-cache penalties.

Closing checklist before sign-off (what I do):
- Verify no pager fires in 10m window after mitigations.
- Post a quick note in #infra-oncall with what I did (commands + time).
- Create/annotate follow-up ticket with root cause breadcrumbs if mitigation was temporary.

Notes to self / TODOs to finish later (this is me talking to future me):
- Flesh out canary gating in PR #2482 — add unit test for prefix-cache hash.
- Move the warming script into a scheduled job that runs for 10m after deploys.
- Add a small section in the formal runbook describing when to prefer fallback-region routing.

If anything breaks badly: breathe. Write timestamped notes in the incident thread (helps a lot).

-- Asha
(last checked 2025-11-03 18:45 UTC)
